words.gloss: the wise / those of sharp intellect

literal: Suddenly at that very moment outwardly they will not boil with anger, the right time having watched, internally they will boil with anger, the wise.
translation: The wise will not show their anger outwardly at the very moment of provocation; instead, they keep it boiling within, waiting for the right time to act.
modern: அறிவுடையவர்கள் தமக்கு ஒரு தீங்கு நேர்ந்த உடனே வெளியில் கோபத்தைக் காட்ட மாட்டார்கள்; தகுந்த காலத்தை எதிர்பார்த்து, அதுவரை கோபத்தை மனத்திற்குள்ளேயே வைத்திருப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains how wise and capable people manage their anger when provoked by an enemy. Instead of reacting instantly and showing their anger outwardly, they keep their resolve and anger burning silently within. They patiently wait for the opportune moment to strike back effectively. The word 'வேர்த்தல்' (literally to sweat) is used here metaphorically to mean boiling or simmering with anger, highlighting the intense but controlled nature of their strategy.
